content.text:
The GPU isn't the problem. The UI thread most likely takes longer than one frame to draw, because every animation frame redraws the whole prompt view, including all of its history.

**GPU and display: fine**
- The app runs on native Wayland (KDE) and draws with wgpu on the AMD Radeon 890M, the same GPU that drives your panel. The Nvidia 4060 is open but idle (P8 power state, 0% use, 2 MiB), so frames aren't being copied between GPUs.
- Your panel is 2880×1800 at 60 Hz with 1.7 scaling. The 890M is at about 19% load, including the desktop, so it has plenty of headroom.

**Why animations drop frames**
To hit 60 fps, each frame has to be ready in 16.6 ms, and most of that work happens on the UI thread. That thread is already 40–70% busy, and here's why:

1. **A running animation redraws the whole view each frame.** In GPUI, `request_animation_frame` and springs redraw the entire view they're in. Nearly everything is one view, `PromptMode` (`src/prompt_mode.rs`, 186 KB). So each frame of the drawer slide, pane slide or dim fade rebuilds:
   - both history accordions: a title row for each of about 250 tasks and 26 questions, built every frame even when collapsed
   - the open task's whole output table
   - the answer drawer and every spring in it

   None of this is virtualized, so frame cost grows with your history, and a long project will feel slower than a new one.
